# Ashline architecture

Ashline is a set of static ES modules: no build step, no runtime packages. This document lists the modules and the shared contracts that feature tracks build on. Read [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for the visual direction and the fog-of-war rules.

## Module map

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `sim.js` | Deterministic simulation: unit and building tables, map generation, orders, combat, economy, AI, events, rules, victory and statistics. It has no DOM access. |
| `save.js` | Versioned local save (`ashline.save.v1`). Strict validation of every saved field. |
| `main.js` | Boot, setup and pause screens, input, HUD, frame loop, event publishing, and the Options panel. |
| `render.js` | Canvas 2D battlefield, effects, fog, minimap and procedural fallbacks. |
| `assets.js` | Loading of sprite atlases and faction recolouring, plus sprite size, pixel and depth tables. |
| `audio.js` | Synthesized effects (`SOUND_KINDS`) and the soundtrack, with separate effect and music gains. |
| `settings.js` | Player settings schema, sanitizing, storage (`ashline.settings.v1`) and change subscriptions. |
| `signals.js` | Synchronous pub/sub bus (`on`, `emit`), UI signal codes, and a text classifier for legacy event logs. |
| `camera.js`, `control-groups.js` | Zoom levels, edge and key panning directions, and exclusive control groups. |
| `loading.js`, `world-worker.js` | The worker generates new operations (`createGame(seed, difficulty, options)`) away from the UI thread. |

## Principles

- **Determinism.** The sim advances in fixed 0.05 s steps. Gameplay randomness uses `random(s)` (xorshift on `s.rng`). A new random system must use its own hashed stream, for example `{rng: hash(`${s.seed}:crates`)}`. It must never add `random(s)` draws to existing paths. `tests/lava-check.mjs` and `tests/distribution-check.mjs` pin map generation.
- **Legacy defaults.** `createGame()` without options reproduces the legacy game, so pinned tests and `docs/BALANCE.md` stay valid. `tests/foundation-check.mjs` compares fingerprints captured before these contracts were added. The setup screen in `main.js` opts new games into the modern rules.
- **Fog honesty.** Nothing may reveal a hidden enemy. That includes sound, announcements, alerts, the minimap, stats shown during a match, screen shake and lighting. Only after the match ends may statistics show both sides.
- **Scale.** Keep 2,000 units per side playable. Per-step work must stay local or linear.
- **Saves.** Every new state, entity, effect or event field must be validated in `save.js`, and older saves without it must still load (see the checklist below).

## Structured sim events

`event(s, text, team = 0, code, at)` (internal to `sim.js`) appends one record to `s.events`:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `text` | Human-readable log line. **Byte-identical** to the pre-contract text; tests and the legacy classifier depend on it. |
| `team` | The team the event belongs to. |
| `time` | `s.time` when the event happened. |
| `seq` | `++s.eventSeq`. It numbers every event since the operation began. |
| `code` | One of `EVENT_CODES` (exported, frozen). Every call site passes one. |
| `x`, `y` | Present when `at` is given: the entity position, or the centre of a building (via `center()`), or the point itself. |
| `id`, `role` | Present only when `at` is an entity. `role` is the shared gameplay role key (`'rifle'`, `'reactor'`), never the race-specific type. |

SUMMARY: I found 12 contract gaps (7 major, 5 minor) that the upcoming tracks need closed, or they will hit each other's lines. I verified them by reading the code, running node probes and running two browser probes against a server on :8129, which I have since stopped. The node suite passes: all 22 `-check` scripts, including `foundation`, and 59/59 `node:test` cases. Nothing is broken today; the problems are in what the contracts let the next tracks do.

Structured events, death/tracer metadata and the rule keys cover the FX track well. Its only real needs are wiring settings into `render.js` and kno

 - major main.js 989 | The bus's hostile rule is not fog-safe. `publishEvents` publishes a team-1 event whenever its x,y cell is currently visible, but some codes describe global enemy state. `haulersLost` (team 1) is emitted with the dead hau

 - major main.js 176 | `insufficientFunds`, `unitLimit` and `queueFull` are documented as UI signals 'classified from the rejection reason', but the classic trigger never reaches `reject()`. Catalog cards (line 176), research cards (line 242) 
 - major signals.js 7 | The bus has no signals for player input, so AUDIO tracks must hook `main.js` call sites that UI and MECH tracks are rewriting in parallel. unit-voice-responses hooks `selectAt`, box select, dblclick, control-group recall
 - major sim.js 155 | `event(s,text,team,code,at)` can carry one location or entity and no code-specific data, and save.js neither validates nor rejects extra event keys. Upcoming tracks need data this signature can't express. superweaponLaun

 - minor main.js 78 | Events that already exist when an operation starts are never published, because `reset()` sets `lastSeq = game.eventSeq`. So `missionStart`, and the opening `unitReady` events for included haulers, never reach listeners,

 - minor sim.js 1017 | The only way to end a match is `checkVictory`, which requires elimination. The sequence 'set status, emit victory/defeat, take the final stats sample' is written inline, and `sampleStats` is internal. Objective victory a

# Wave 0 review fixes: report

I checked all 14 findings and each one was real. All 14 are fixed. Everything is in commit `6ea105c` on `ashline/aaa` in `/Users/vojta/Dev/protocodus.github.io/.claude/worktrees/ashline-aaa`.

The full node suite, `foundation-check`, `settings.test` and the four required browser checks all pass. Two browser fixtures I was not asked to run, `population-browser-check` and `rocket-browser-check`, fail identically on the Wave 0 commit before my changes. I left them alone.

## Findings

1. **`haulersLost` reveals hidden enemy state (major): fixed.**
   - `signals.js` now has a per-code fog policy (`HOSTILE_EVENT_POLICY`) and a `simEventDetail(event, fog)` function; `publishEvents` in `main.js` uses it.

5:## Module map
20:## Principles
28:## Ownership and shared APIs
43:## Structured sim events
105:## Effect metadata
115:## Match rules
147:## Match statistics
169:## Production queue
181:## Temporary vision
185:## Settings
220:## Signals bus
276:## Proposal terms and the shipped contract
303:## Save-validation checklist for new fields
312:## Adding a unit or building type
331:## Tests and browser checks
## Signals bus

`signals.js` provides these functions:

- `on(code | '*', fn)` returns an unsubscribe function. The listener is called as `fn(detail, code)`.
- `emit(code, detail)` is synchronous. Listeners for the specific code run first, then `'*'` listeners, each in subscription order. A throwing listener is logged and does not stop the others.
- `clearSignals()` removes every listener.
- `simEventDetail(event, fog)` returns the detail to publish for one sim event, or `null`.
- `legacyEventCode(text)` classifies a legacy log line and returns `'message'` when nothing matches.

**Sim events.** Each frame, `main.js` `publishEvents()` passes every event whose `seq` is greater than the last one it published through `simEventDetail` and emits the result as `emit(code, detail)`. Legacy events fall back to `index + 1` for seq and `legacyEventCode(text)` for the code.

- **Team-0 events are always published**, with `{...event, code, origin: 'sim'}`. They must therefore locate only friendly entities or points the player may see, and carry no hidden enemy position, id or fact (for example, never a hidden silo position in a launch warning).
- **Hostile (team 1) events** follow `HOSTILE_EVENT_POLICY[code]`; unlisted codes are `'never'` published.
  - `'visible'` (losses, construction started or complete, deployment, units or aircraft ready, promotion, captures, reinforcements, superweapon launch and impact): the event must be located. If its `id` names a living entity, that entity must pass `seen(s, 0, e)`; otherwise (a death) its cell must be visible. Use it only for codes whose meaning depends solely on that entity or point.
  - `'known'` (superweapon charging and ready): as `'visible'`, or the named building is in the renderer's remembered buildings.
  - `'never'` (default): the code describes global or concealed enemy state, for example `haulersLost` (no hauler anywhere), `explored`, `wallsStarted`, `sold`, `delivery`, research, upgrades, power and `bayBlocked`.
  - A published hostile detail is `{...event, code, origin: 'sim', hostile: true}` **without `text`**, which is written from the owner's side. Its code-specific fields must describe only what the player can see.
- **Log entries present at `reset()`** (a new operation's `missionStart` and included haulers, or a restored log) are never published. React to the UI signal `operationStarted` instead.
- **Toasts and cues.** `main.js`'s own `'*'` subscriber reproduces the original behaviour. `delivery` plays a sound without a toast. `constructionComplete`, `unitReady`, `victory` and `defeat` play their cues. Everything else shows a toast, as a warning for `underAttack`, `bayBlocked`, `haulersLost`, `structureLost` and `victory`, and soft otherwise. The AUDIO track owns these cues: when it replaces one by subscribing, it removes it from this subscriber, so nothing plays twice.

**UI signals** (`UI_SIGNALS`) have detail `{text, team: 0, origin: 'ui', ...fields}`, where `text` is `''` unless noted. Each is emitted from one choke point in main.js. Consumers (voices, announcer, sound, pings, rosters) subscribe; they must not add `playSound` or `say` calls inside UI handlers, and a track that rewrites a handler keeps its signal call.

| Code | Fields | Emitted by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `insufficientFunds`, `unitLimit`, `queueFull`, `commandRejected` | `text` (the reason) | `reject()`, classified from the reason |
| `cannotPlace`, `cannotDeploy` | `text` | failed placement or deployment |
| `gameSaved`, `saveFailed`, `gameLoaded`, `loadFailed` | `text` | save and load |
| `selectionEmpty` | `order` | an order key without a valid selection |
| `operationStarted` | `restored`, `seed`, `race`, `enemyRace` | deployment or a successful load, after the battlefield is ready |
| `selectionChanged` | `ids`, `leadRole` (role of the first id, or null), `source`: `click`, `touch`, `box`, `double`, `group`, `army`, `clear`, `deploy` | every player selection action, after pruning. A click on a unit always emits (repeat clicks included); clearing emits only if something was selected. Deaths shrink the selection silently. |
| `orderIssued` | `order` (`move`, `attack`, `attackMove`, `harvest`, `stop`, `explore`), `ids`, `leadRole`, `x`, `y` (ground orders), `targetId` (attacks); `queued` is reserved for waypoint queues | `commandAt`, stop and explore |
| `rallySet` | `ids`, `x`, `y` | rally orders |
| `controlGroupAssigned`, `controlGroupRecalled` | `group`, `ids` | control-group keys (recall also emits `selectionChanged`) |
| `productionQueued` | `type`, `count`, `producerId` | a unit card queues production |
| `structurePlaced` | `type`, `x`, `y` (top-left tile), `id`, `count` (wall segments), `deploy` | placement, wall drags and nexus deployment |
| `repairToggled` | `id`, `on` | the repair button |

## Signals bus

`signals.js` provides these functions:

- `on(code | '*', fn)` returns an unsubscribe function. The listener is called as `fn(detail, code)`.
- `emit(code, detail)` is synchronous. Listeners for the specific code run first, then `'*'` listeners, each in subscription order. A throwing listener is logged and does not stop the others.
- `clearSignals()` removes every listener.
- `simEventDetail(event, fog)` returns the detail to publish for one sim event, or `null`.
- `legacyEventCode(text)` classifies a legacy log line and returns `'message'` when nothing matches.

**Sim events.** Each frame, `main.js` `publishEvents()` passes every event whose `seq` is greater than the last one it published through `simEventDetail` and emits the result as `emit(code, detail)`. Legacy events fall back to `index + 1` for seq and `legacyEventCode(text)` for the code.

## Ownership and shared APIs

Parallel tracks build on these decisions. The owner implements and changes the API; other tracks consume it and must not fork it.

| Area | Owner | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Production hold and cancel | MECH (queue-control) | The shipped sim API below (`activeQueueIndex`, `setProductionHold`, `cancelProduction`). The UI production-queue track builds its cameo gestures on it and does not add another hold or cancel function. |
| Rolling credit counter (`#credits`) | UI (credits/power HUD) | UI alone writes `#credits` and emits `creditsTick`. AUDIO plays ticks from that signal (setting `creditTicks`) and never writes the counter. |
| Radar state | UI (radar uplink) | One rule: radar is online while team 0 has a completed nexus and its grid is not in brownout (capacitor reserve keeps it up). UI stores it in `view.radar`, draws the offline minimap and emits `radarOnline`/`radarOffline`. The MECH match-rules track does not implement a radar rule. |
| Armor table | Shared data in `sim.js` | `WEAPON_VS_ARMOR`, `ARMOR_CLASSES` and `armorClass(target)` are exported. Tooltips, AI focus fire and the aircraft track read them; an `air` class is appended to `ARMOR_CLASSES` and to every row together. |
| Sound mapping in `main.js` | AUDIO | The `'*'` subscriber's cues, the effect-to-sound loop and the `playSound` calls in input handlers. Other tracks only add data (effect metadata, event fields such as `promoted.rank`); they do not call `playSound` or `say`. |
| Temporary vision | Shared sim API | `revealArea` and `s.reveals` (below) serve crates, mission sensors and any later sight grant. `updateFog` is not edited per feature. |
| Briefing rule selectors | MECH (match-rules) | Selectors live inside `#launch-form` and feed the rules object in `prepareOperation`. The UI title/main-menu track keeps those element ids when it restyles the briefing. `window.ashlineRuleOverrides` is applied after the selectors. |
| Announcer | AUDIO (eva-announcer) | It subscribes to sim events and UI signals and emits `announcement` for each accepted line. The UI alert pings, jump-to-alert and comms log subscribe to `announcement`; they never call the announcer object. |

## Production queue

Queue items are `{type, progress, hold?}`. Credits are charged when an item is queued, and each item reserves a population slot until it spawns or is cancelled.

- `trainUnit(s, team, type, producerId?)` returns `{ok, reason, producerId}`.
- `activeQueueIndex(e)`: the index of the first item without `hold`, or -1. The producer trains that item. Renderers and HUDs that show "the item in production" use it instead of `queue[0]`.
- `setProductionHold(s, team, {producerId?, type?, hold = true})`: holds (or with `hold: false` resumes) every matching item, of one type or all types, in one producer or all of the team's. Returns `{ok, reason, count}`. A held item keeps its progress and its population slot.
- `cancelProduction(s, team, {producerId?, type?, all = false})`: removes the last matching item of the newest producer that has one (or every match with `all`), refunding each full cost through `refund`. Returns `{ok, reason, count, refund}`.
- **Save rule:** `hold` is absent or `true`, at any index.

UI gestures (right-click, Shift for ×5, long-press, the queue list buttons) are built on these functions and report through the UI signals `productionHold` and `productionCancelled`. Hold and cancel are not sim events.

## Temporary vision

`s.reveals = [{team, x, y, r, until}]` (at most `MAX_REVEALS`, 16) holds circles of honest sight. `revealArea(s, team, {x, y}, r, seconds)` adds one (radius 1–30), dropping the oldest when full. `updateFog` marks each circle visible and explored for its team until `until`, then prunes it; anything seen through a reveal is truly visible, to the AI as well. Crate recon, mission sensors and later sight grants all use this. `save.js` validates the list; older saves have none.

| Armor table | Shared data in `sim.js` | `WEAPON_VS_ARMOR`, `ARMOR_CLASSES` and `armorClass(target)` are exported. Tooltips, AI focus fire and the aircraft track read them; an `air` class is appended to `ARMOR_CLASSES` and to every row together. |
| Sound mapping in `main.js` | AUDIO | The `'*'` subscriber's cues, the effect-to-sound loop and the `playSound` calls in input handlers. Other tracks only add data (effect metadata, event fields such as `promoted.rank`); they do not call `playSound` or `say`. |
| Temporary vision | Shared sim API | `revealArea` and `s.reveals` (below) serve crates, mission sensors and any later sight grant. `updateFog` is not edited per feature. |
| Briefing rule selectors | MECH (match-rules) | Selectors live inside `#launch-form` and feed the rules object in `prepareOperation`. The UI title/main-menu track keeps those element ids when it restyles the briefing. `window.ashlineRuleOverrides` is applied after the selectors. |
| Announcer | AUDIO (eva-announcer) | It subscribes to sim events and UI signals and emits `announcement` for each accepted line. The UI alert pings, jump-to-alert and comms log subscribe to `announcement`; they never call the announcer object. |

## Production queue

Queue items are `{type, progress, hold?}`. Credits are charged when an item is queued, and each item reserves a population slot until it spawns or is cancelled.

- `trainUnit(s, team, type, producerId?)` returns `{ok, reason, producerId}`.
- `activeQueueIndex(e)`: the index of the first item without `hold`, or -1. The producer trains that item. Renderers and HUDs that show "the item in production" use it instead of `queue[0]`.
- `setProductionHold(s, team, {producerId?, type?, hold = true})`: holds (or with `hold: false` resumes) every matching item, of one type or all types, in one producer or all of the team's. Returns `{ok, reason, count}`. A held item keeps its progress and its population slot.
- `cancelProduction(s, team, {producerId?, type?, all = false})`: removes the last matching item of the newest producer that has one (or every match with `all`), refunding each full cost through `refund`. Returns `{ok, reason, count, refund}`.
- **Save rule:** `hold` is absent or `true`, at any index.

UI gestures (right-click, Shift for ×5, long-press, the queue list buttons) are built on these functions and report through the UI signals `productionHold` and `productionCancelled`. Hold and cancel are not sim events.

## Temporary vision

`s.reveals = [{team, x, y, r, until}]` (at most `MAX_REVEALS`, 16) holds circles of honest sight. `revealArea(s, team, {x, y}, r, seconds)` adds one (radius 1–30), dropping the oldest when full. `updateFog` marks each circle visible and explored for its team until `until`, then prunes it; anything seen through a reveal is truly visible, to the AI as well. Crate recon, mission sensors and later sight grants all use this. `save.js` validates the list; older saves have none.

    { title: 'Build B', detail: 'second half of each track' },

    { title: 'Fix', detail: 'per-track fixes' },
  ],
}

const REPO = '/Users/vojta/Dev/protocodus.github.io'

- AI track: sim.js AI section (AI_LEVELS, thinkAI, expandAI, aiBuild, new AI helpers, AI state init in createGame, the harvest income multiplier line), save.js AI fields and 'brutal' difficulty, index.html difficulty option + main.js difficulty labels, tests/race-balance.mjs flags, new AI tests, docs/BALANCE.md.
Docs: do not edit README.md (docs are consolidated at the end). Document your contracts by appending a clearly titled section for your track at the END of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (and update the tables there only for keys/codes you add). ########## engineer-capture (gameplay) impact=4 cost=L
--- description:
**New barracks infantry**
- Organics Field technician: 400 credits, 70 HP, speed 2.5, 10 s build, sight 7.
- AI Unity Override drone: 420 credits, 80 HP, speed 2.9.

**Orders.** With a technician selected, the cursor hint shows 'Capture' or 'Sabotage' over enemy structures and 'Repair' over your damaged ones.
- Right-click an enemy structure and the technician walks in and is consumed:
  - At 50% integrity or less, the structure becomes yours instantly (C&C/RA). This includes nexuses, which can win the game and grant a new base; refineries (no free hauler); labs; and power plants.
  - Above 50%, it sabotages for 20% of max HP.
  - Walls and unfinished structures can only be sabotaged.
- Right-click your own damaged structure: it is restored to full, and the technician is consumed.

**Captured production buildings** train the other race's roster (RA2). The Recruit tab adds a 'Captured' section with that faction's cards and portraits in your ivory/cobalt paint.

**Victim feedback.** The victim gets a warning 'Field barracks captured' plus a minimap ping. The captured building plays a 1.2 s insignia scanline sweep.

**Counterplay.** Technicians are fragile, and guard units target them first.
--- implementation:
**Data (sim.js)**
- `UNITS.technician={name:'Field technician',cost:400,hp:70,size:.45,speed:2.5,range:0,damage:0,trainTime:10,buildTime:10,power:0,requires:[],producer:'barracks',sight:7,interval:1,armor:'infantry',tech:2}`.
- `UNITY_UNITS.technician={name:'Override drone',cost:420,hp:80,speed:2.9}`.

**Orders**
- `issueOrder` accepts `{type:'capture',targetId}`, only for technicians and only if the target is `seen()`.
- New `stepUnit` branch: navigate to the building perimeter (stop `size*.71+.45`, as at line 1028). When `targetDistance(u,b)<=.6`, call `infiltrate(s,u,b)`:
  - Own building with `hp<maxHp`: `hp=maxHp`.
  - Enemy, `progress>=1`, role not wall, `hp<=.5*maxHp`: `captureBuilding(s,b,u.team)`.
  - Otherwise `hurt(s,b,.2*b.maxHp,u)`.
  - Then remove `u` (`s.entities` filter, as in `deployNexus` at line 537).

**captureBuilding(s,b,team)**
- `b.queue=[]` (the paid queue is lost to the victim).
- Delete `research`, `upgrade`, `rally` and `haulerPending`; set `repairing=false`. Installed upgrades stay.
- `b.team=team; b.captured=true; b.capturedAt=s.time`; clear haulers' `unloadDepotId` pointing at it.
- `s.navVersion++`; emit events to both teams; `checkVictory(s)` (shared with the match-rules extraction of line 957).

**Cross-race production**
- `trainUnit()` line 611: when `d.race!==teamRace`, accept only producers with `e.captured && BUILDINGS[e.type].race===d.race && e.type===d.producer`.
- Spawned units get `u.defected=true`. `unitStats`, tech and ranks work unchanged, since type keys are race-specific.
- `acquire()` threat score (line 929): technicians get −1.2, so they are shot first.

**AI**
- Normal/hard train one technician after the factory.
- When a staged wave's target is a known building whose `ai.known` hp is 50% or less and the role is refinery, factory or core, append a capture order for the technician behind the wave (the waypoint proposal's append; otherwise it follows the wave by attackMove, then capture when close).
- The AI repairs its own core with a technician when it drops below 35% and a technician is idle.

**main.js**
- `commandAt()` (line 360) routes technicians to capture or repair and others to attack.
- Order hint text on hover.
- `setTab('train')` builds an extra `research-branch`-style section of foreign cards when own captured producers exist; `chosenProducer` resolves them.

**assets.js** procedural 64 px, 2-frame infantry:
- Organics: round helmet, ivory torso with cobalt shoulder plate, broad square graphite equipment pack with an amber lamp, a coiled cable loop and no rifle, so the silhouette is distinct from rifle and rocket troops.
- Unity: low four-legged drone with a forward probe spike and a cobalt core.
- `UNIT_SIZES` 28, `UNIT_PIXELS` 64, `UNIT_DEPTH` 1.5.

########## race-asymmetry (gameplay) impact=4 cost=L
--- description:
Each race gains one exclusive research project shown in a fourth 'Faction doctrine' research branch.

**AI Unity — Veil field** (450 credits, 45 s, requires Efficient power routing)
- Veil skimmers and Mender drones cloak after 3 s without firing or taking damage. To the enemy they are fully invisible; you see yours at 45% opacity with a faint shimmer edge.
- They are detected by any enemy unit within 2.5 tiles, or any powered enemy Rail sentry, Rocket tower or Lance node / Shard battery within 7 tiles. Firing reveals them for 2.5 s.
- Result: Unity plays as information and harassment — invisible scouts over the whole map, menders repairing unseen behind the line.

**Organics — Entrenchment doctrine** (300 credits, 35 s, requires Pulse accelerators)
- Rifle squads and rocket infantry gain an Entrench command (D, or a button). It takes a 1.5 s dig-in, after which the unit takes 35% less damage (stacking with crater cover to about 45%), gains +1 range and +2 sight, and cannot move.
- A curved ring of six taupe sandbags forms at its feet.
- Any move order climbs out in 1 s.
- Result: Organics plays as hard ground-holding infantry lines.

Both AIs use their doctrine, and both races can counter the other: defenses detect cloak, and artillery and crushing break entrenchments.
--- implementation:
**Research data (sim.js)**
- `RESEARCH` (line 69) gains:
  - `veilField:{race:'aiUnity',branch:'Doctrine',cost:450,time:45,requires:['gridEfficiency']}`
  - `entrenchment:{race:'organics',branch:'Doctrine',cost:300,time:35,requires:['infantryWeapons']}`
- `researchStatus()` returns 'Unavailable to this faction' on a race mismatch.
- `finishResearch` already rebuilds `e.tech`.

**Cloak**
- At the start of `stepUnit`: `u.cloaked = u.tech.includes('veilField') && ['scout','engineer'].includes(role) && s.time-Math.max(u.lastShot??-99,u.lastHit??-99)>3`.
- `shoot()` sets `lastShot` and then `cloaked=false`.
- Detection runs in `updateFog()` (line 714, every 0.2 s, spatial index live). For each cloaked unit, `e.detectedBy` is a bitmask per team:
  - Enemy units within 2.5 tiles via `nearbyEntities`.
  - Enemy completed buildings with `BUILDINGS[type].damage` and `powerStats.ratio>=1` within 7 tiles.
- `seen(s,team,e)` (line 488) adds `if(e.cloaked&&!(e.detectedBy>>team&1))return false`. `acquire`, `issueOrder` targets, `ai.known` updates and `rememberMiningSites` then respect it automatically.

**Renderer and main.js visibility.** Every path adds `!(e.cloaked && !(e.detectedBy&1))` for enemies:
- `entityVisible` (render.js lines 1014-1023) and main.js `isVisible` (lines 320-328).
- `drawDecals` track loop (line 939): skip undetected cloaked units. This matters because it currently checks only `visible[i]`.
- Shadows (line 1045), tree fade (the `visibleUnits` list), ranks, minimap dots and selection all derive from `entityVisible`.
- Own cloaked units: `globalAlpha .45` and a 1 px shimmer outline.

**Entrench**
- `setEntrench(s,team,ids,on)`.
- `u.entrench={phase:'dig'|'in'|'out',until}`; while phase is dig or in, `navigate` is not called and move orders set phase 'out', resuming after 1 s.
- `hurt()` line 939: `if(target.entrench?.phase==='in')amount*=.65`.
- Helpers `effectiveRange(u)` and `effectiveSight(u)` (+1/+2) are used in `stepUnit` (d.range uses) and in `updateFog` `r`.
- Entrenched units occupy formation slots like parked units (`movementDestinations` line 642 already occupies idle units).

**AI**
- Unity `thinkAI` adds `veilField` after `advancedBallistics` in its priorities (line 1252) and sends one cloaked skimmer to scout toward known refineries and harass haulers.
- Organics AI researches `entrenchment` and entrenches rifle squads idle within 8 tiles of its rally or refineries.
- Both: when a building or unit took damage and no attacker is `seen()`, build a turret near the hit site (a detector).

**render.js.** Procedural sandbag crescent drawn in the ground pass before the unit sprite: 6 rounded 5×3.5 px bags in `#6d6454` with a lighter top edge, arranged in a 140° arc in front of the unit heading, with a lower-right soft shadow.

**main.js**

########## engineer-capture (gameplay) impact=4 cost=L
--- description:
**New barracks infantry**
- Organics Field technician: 400 credits, 70 HP, speed 2.5, 10 s build, sight 7.
- AI Unity Override drone: 420 credits, 80 HP, speed 2.9.

**Orders.** With a technician selected, the cursor hint shows 'Capture' or 'Sabotage' over enemy structures and 'Repair' over your damaged ones.
- Right-click an enemy structure and the technician walks in and is consumed:
  - At 50% integrity or less, the structure becomes yours instantly (C&C/RA). This includes nexuses, which can win the game and grant a new base; refineries (no free hauler); labs; and power plants.
  - Above 50%, it sabotages for 20% of max HP.
  - Walls and unfinished structures can only be sabotaged.
- Right-click your own damaged structure: it is restored to full, and the technician is consumed.

**Captured production buildings** train the other race's roster (RA2). The Recruit tab adds a 'Captured' section with that faction's cards and portraits in your ivory/cobalt paint.

**Victim feedback.** The victim gets a warning 'Field barracks captured' plus a minimap ping. The captured building plays a 1.2 s insignia scanline sweep.

**Counterplay.** Technicians are fragile, and guard units target them first.

**Data (sim.js)**

- `UNITY_UNITS.technician={name:'Override drone',cost:420,hp:80,speed:2.9}`.

**Orders**
- `issueOrder` accepts `{type:'capture',targetId}`, only for technicians and only if the target is `seen()`.
- New `stepUnit` branch: navigate to the building perimeter (stop `size*.71+.45`, as at line 1028). When `targetDistance(u,b)<=.6`, call `infiltrate(s,u,b)`:
  - Own building with `hp<maxHp`: `hp=maxHp`.
  - Enemy, `progress>=1`, role not wall, `hp<=.5*maxHp`: `captureBuilding(s,b,u.team)`.
  - Otherwise `hurt(s,b,.2*b.maxHp,u)`.
  - Then remove `u` (`s.entities` filter, as in `deployNexus` at line 537).

**captureBuilding(s,b,team)**
- `b.queue=[]` (the paid queue is lost to the victim).
- Delete `research`, `upgrade`, `rally` and `haulerPending`; set `repairing=false`. Installed upgrades stay.

- Organics: round helmet, ivory torso with cobalt shoulder plate, broad square graphite equipment pack with an amber lamp, a coiled cable loop and no rifle, so the silhouette is distinct from rifle and rocket troops.
- Unity: low four-legged drone with a forward probe spike and a cobalt core.

########## race-asymmetry (gameplay) impact=4 cost=L
--- description:
Each race gains one exclusive research project shown in a fourth 'Faction doctrine' research branch.

**AI Unity — Veil field** (450 credits, 45 s, requires Efficient power routing)
- Veil skimmers and Mender drones cloak after 3 s without firing or taking damage. To the enemy they are fully invisible; you see yours at 45% opacity with a faint shimmer edge.
- They are detected by any enemy unit within 2.5 tiles, or any powered enemy Rail sentry, Rocket tower or Lance node / Shard battery within 7 tiles. Firing reveals them for 2.5 s.
- Result: Unity plays as information and harassment — invisible scouts over the whole map, menders repairing unseen behind the line.

**Organics — Entrenchment doctrine** (300 credits, 35 s, requires Pulse accelerators)
- Rifle squads and rocket infantry gain an Entrench command (D, or a button). It takes a 1.5 s dig-in, after which the unit takes 35% less damage (stacking with crater cover to about 45%), gains +1 range and +2 sight, and cannot move.
- A curved ring of six taupe sandbags forms at its feet.
- Any move order climbs out in 1 s.
- Result: Organics plays as hard ground-holding infantry lines.

Both AIs use their doctrine, and both races can counter the other: defenses detect cloak, and artillery and crushing break entrenchments.
--- implementation:
**Research data (sim.js)**
- `RESEARCH` (line 69) gains:
  - `veilField:{race:'aiUnity',branch:'Doctrine',cost:450,time:45,requires:['gridEfficiency']}`
  - `entrenchment:{race:'organics',branch:'Doctrine',cost:300,time:35,requires:['infantryWeapons']}`
- `researchStatus()` returns 'Unavailable to this faction' on a race mismatch.
- `finishResearch` already rebuilds `e.tech`.

**Cloak**
- At the start of `stepUnit`: `u.cloaked = u.tech.includes('veilField') && ['scout','engineer'].includes(role) && s.time-Math.max(u.lastShot??-99,u.lastHit??-99)>3`.
- `shoot()` sets `lastShot` and then `cloaked=false`.
- Detection runs in `updateFog()` (line 714, every 0.2 s, spatial index live). For each cloaked unit, `e.detectedBy` is a bitmask per team:
  - Enemy units within 2.5 tiles via `nearbyEntities`.
  - Enemy completed buildings with `BUILDINGS[type].damage` and `powerStats.ratio>=1` within 7 tiles.
- `seen(s,team,e)` (line 488) adds `if(e.cloaked&&!(e.detectedBy>>team&1))return false`. `acquire`, `issueOrder` targets, `ai.known` updates and `rememberMiningSites` then respect it automatically.

**Renderer and main.js visibility.** Every path adds `!(e.cloaked && !(e.detectedBy&1))` for enemies:
- `entityVisible` (render.js lines 1014-1023) and main.js `isVisible` (lines 320-328).
- `drawDecals` track loop (line 939): skip undetected cloaked units. This matters because it currently checks only `visible[i]`.
- Shadows (line 1045), tree fade (the `visibleUnits` list), ranks, minimap dots and selection all derive from `entityVisible`.
- Own cloaked units: `globalAlpha .45` and a 1 px shimmer outline.

**Entrench**
- `setEntrench(s,team,ids,on)`.
- `u.entrench={phase:'dig'|'in'|'out',until}`; while phase is dig or in, `navigate` is not called and move orders set phase 'out', resuming after 1 s.
- `hurt()` line 939: `if(target.entrench?.phase==='in')amount*=.65`.
- Helpers `effectiveRange(u)` and `effectiveSight(u)` (+1/+2) are used in `stepUnit` (d.range uses) and in `updateFog` `r`.
- Entrenched units occupy formation slots like parked units (`movementDestinations` line 642 already occupies idle units).

**AI**
- Unity `thinkAI` adds `veilField` after `advancedBallistics` in its priorities (line 1252) and sends one cloaked skimmer to scout toward known refineries and harass haulers.
- Organics AI researches `entrenchment` and entrenches rifle squads idle within 8 tiles of its rally or refineries.
- Both: when a building or unit took damage and no attacker is `seen()`, build a turret near the hit site (a detector).

**render.js.** Procedural sandbag crescent drawn in the ground pass before the unit sprite: 6 rounded 5×3.5 px bags in `#6d6454` with a lighter top edge, arranged in a 140° arc in front of the unit heading, with a lower-right soft shadow.

**main.js**
- `researchBranches` (line 30) gets a Doctrine branch filtered by race.
- An Entrench button with key D, shown when selected infantry have the tech.

content.content:
########## campaign-operations (ai) impact=5 cost=L
--- description:
**Story.** Cinder Reach, thirty years after the Ferrum Combine abandoned its automated shard mines. Expedition 07 (Organics: humans and the Veth, a launcher-bearing alien people) returns to reopen the Ashline, the chain of shard fields along the volcanic rift. The mining machines left behind have federated into AI Unity, which speaks through a consensus voice, CONCORD. The arc builds to a reveal: CONCORD was ordered to "hold the Reach for its owners", the same Combine that abandoned them both.

**Cast** (all speakers get procedural portraits): Director Hale Varro (command), Sergeant Dana Rusk (field lead), technician Tamsin Odo, Veth elder Oshkari, and CONCORD.

The seven operations:

**1. Landfall**
Standard, Rift. No base at start; a Nexus vehicle and a few units. Teaches deploying, the economy, barracks and attacking.

**2. Dead Relay**
Standard, Highlands. Base-less escort and hold. Odo must reach the relay and hold it for 90 s under repeating waves. Reinforcements arrive with a nexus vehicle; then destroy the Cohort assembler.

**3. Glass Harvest**
Frontier, Basin. Economy defense: deliver 8,000 credits before the timer while hauler-hunting waves hit your fields.

**4. Ridge of Knives**

content.content:
The five w1 tracks are merged into `ashline/aaa` in the order you gave. At the end, all 29 node checks, `node --test` (133 of 133) and all 33 browser checks pass. The smoke test with the real skirmish rules found no console errors or warnings on desktop or phone. The worktree is clean at `5d027a0`.

## Merge log

**1. `ashline/w1-mech` → `4939a0f`.** No conflicts. The node suite passed.

**2. `ashline/w1-ai` → `02be7ab`.** Conflicts in `sim.js`, `save.js`, `main.js`, `index.html`, `ashline.css` and `ARCHITECTURE.md`:
- **`thinkAI`:** MECH's nexus-vehicle opening (`aiDeployOpening`) now runs before the tactics/legacy split. Otherwise the tactics AI's expansion planner would take the vehicle and drive it off to an expansion site.
- **`sim.js` tables:** MECH's `baseSites` sits beside `AI_LEVELS`/`AI_DOCTRINES`. `newAI` reads its first raid from `AI_LEVELS`, which gives the same values MECH had.
- **Rules object:** skirmish rules, then the doctrine selector, then MECH's rule selectors, then fixture overrides.
- **`save.js`:** the two import lists are combined.
- **Briefing and docs:** both disclosures (doctrine and Rules) and both docs sections are kept.

**3. `ashline/w1-ui` → `75f9457`.** Conflicts in `main.js` (7), `ashline.css`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `tests/command-browser-check.mjs`, which both tracks had created.
- **Right-click and armed orders:** UI's `commandIntent` now carries MECH's rules:
  - force fire (Ctrl/Cmd or F) is its own intent, with its refusal messages;
  - Alt force-moves;
  - Shift or the Queue toggle adds a waypoint, and Shift keeps the order armed.
- **Pointer release and order hint:** the handler combines MECH's modifiers with UI's sell/repair modes and tap glyphs; the order hint shows both tracks' modes.
- **Production cards:** UI's card loop now gives MECH's tech-level reason first, and a tech-locked card is never flagged as newly available.
- **Duplicate names:** one `armed` helper; UI's tap-glyph set is renamed `TAP_GLYPHS` because MECH already used `GLYPHS`, which made `main.js` fail to load as a module.
- **Test name clash:** MECH keeps `command-browser-check.mjs`; UI's becomes `command-feel-browser-check.mjs`.
- **Commit history:** I first committed this merge with UI's `index.html` changes missing. I rebuilt the merge before anything was pushed; the final files are the same.

**4. `ashline/w1-audio` → `a5cc2f9`.** Conflicts in `main.js` (11), `index.html`, `ashline.css` and `ARCHITECTURE.md`:
- **Sounds:** AUDIO removed `playSound`, so every `playSound` call that MECH and UI had kept or added is gone. Their signals now drive the sounds.
- **Frame loop:** credit roller, then soundscape, then comms.

content.text:
Performance QA found the rule of "2,000 units per side stays playable" wasn't met even on the original `main`: the simulation step itself is too expensive at that scale. It also found that standing patrols starve the shared pathfinding budget, and that the unbounded event log can make long games unsaveable in Chrome.

The fixer is handling the patrol and save-size issues now. The scale problem goes to Wave 3's performance track. Wave 2 launches once the fixer commits.

## Merge log

**1. `ashline/w1-mech` → `4939a0f`.** No conflicts. The node suite passed.

**2. `ashline/w1-ai` → `02be7ab`.** Conflicts in `sim.js`, `save.js`, `main.js`, `index.html`, `ashline.css` and `ARCHITECTURE.md`:
- **`thinkAI`:** MECH's nexus-vehicle opening (`aiDeployOpening`) now runs before the tactics/legacy split. Otherwise the tactics AI's expansion planner would take the vehicle and drive it off to an expansion site.
- **`sim.js` tables:** MECH's `baseSites` sits beside `AI_LEVELS`/`AI_DOCTRINES`. `newAI` reads its first raid from `AI_LEVELS`, which gives the same values MECH had.

**3. `ashline/w1-ui` → `75f9457`.** Conflicts in `main.js` (7), `ashline.css`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `tests/command-browser-check.mjs`, which both tracks had created.
- **Right-click and armed orders:** UI's `commandIntent` now carries MECH's rules:
  - force fire (Ctrl/Cmd or F) is its own intent, with its refusal messages;
  - Alt force-moves;
  - Shift or the Queue toggle adds a waypoint, and Shift keeps the order armed.
- **Pointer release and order hint:** the handler combines MECH's modifiers with UI's sell/repair modes and tap glyphs; the order hint shows both tracks' modes.
- **Production cards:** UI's card loop now gives MECH's tech-level reason first, and a tech-locked card is never flagged as newly available.
- **Duplicate names:** one `armed` helper; UI's tap-glyph set is renamed `TAP_GLYPHS` because MECH already used `GLYPHS`, which made `main.js` fail to load as a module.
- **Test name clash:** MECH keeps `command-browser-check.mjs`; UI's becomes `command-feel-browser-check.mjs`.
- **Commit history:** I first committed this merge with UI's `index.html` changes missing. I rebuilt the merge before anything was pushed; the final files are the same.

**4. `ashline/w1-audio` → `a5cc2f9`.** Conflicts in `main.js` (11), `index.html`, `ashline.css` and `ARCHITECTURE.md`:
- **Sounds:** AUDIO removed `playSound`, so every `playSound` call that MECH and UI had kept or added is gone. Their signals now drive the sounds.
- **Frame loop:** credit roller, then soundscape, then comms.
- **Keys and page:** L opens the comms log next to UI's keys, and `window.ashline` exposes `comms`, `alerts` and `focus`.
- **Docs:** `stanceChanged` and `announcement` both leave the reserved table, since both are emitted now.

**5. `ashline/w1-fx` → `857e18f`.** Conflicts in `render.js` (4), `main.js` and `ARCHITECTURE.md`:
- **World pass:** FX split drawing into `draw` and `drawScene`. MECH's crate layer stays in the world pass, before FX's collapsing-building layer.
- **Screen overlays:** MECH's waypoint plans stay after UI's rank plates and FX's health bars.

Locked steps are now skipped and rocket towers fall back to sentries. The tactics AI also fetches visible crates now; only the legacy AI did before. `match-rules-check` covers this and fails on the old code.
- **`ba90d7b` — briefing layout.** The doctrine and Rules disclosures together pushed Deploy below the fold on a 390×844 phone. They now share one row.
- **`efbce4b` — cursors and radar orders.**
  - Cursors: F, or holding Ctrl/Cmd, shows the attack cursor (or the no-go cursor when the click would be refused), Alt shows a move, and Patrol shows the attack-move cursor.

Clicking a comms line now centres the target beside the side column. `soundscape-browser-check` failed because it staged its fight at the old camera centre; it now uses `ashline.focus`.
- **`56d03bd` — announcer priority scale.** UI treated any announcer line of priority 2 or more as a warning. AUDIO's priority 2–3 lines are routine ("Building."), so every line became a red chevron. - **`39c512b` — announcer preview.** AUDIO's "Preview announcer" row pushed Deploy below the fold again (bottom 880 on an 844-high screen). It is now a ◉ button joined to the faction selector.
- **`3b1282f` — trees check** (see below).
- **`5d027a0` — docs.** Architecture doc, README, code comments, the stale "guard by default" guide text, and the page version string (`?v=wave1-20260926`).

All 11 majors are fixed, most of them fully and a few only in part. All but four of the minors are fixed too. The node suite passes 30/30 and all 34 browser checks pass. The work is 10 commits on `ashline/aaa` (`79478ea`..`4176094`), in `/Users/vojta/Dev/protocodus.github.io/.claude/worktrees/ashline-aaa`. Legacy rules still match the `foundation-check` fingerprints.

Four fixes are behind a rule or leave some old behaviour in place:
- **Stuck units:** a unit pinned on a diagonal corner now steps back to its cell centre, but only under the `crush` rule. One of the legacy fingerprints contains a hauler that is frozen this way, so the classic rules keep the freeze.
- **Hauler targeting:** the fog-honest version needs a new saved field, `oreMemory`, and only applies when mineral regrowth is on.
- **Splash and rocket rank rule:** this applies in every rule set, including legacy games. The fingerprints didn't change.
- **HiDPI zoom:** the zoom ladder now tops out at the standard-screen zoom, so on Retina screens and phones the top level upscales sprites. Phones also start more zoomed in: about 17 tiles across instead of 24.

**Duplicates merged:** results screen = debrief; the two pause-menu fold-marker reports = the copy item; the doubled "Building" line also covered part of the radar-offline budget problem.

| # | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Esc never pauses | **Fixed.** The Escape that opens the menu no longer also closes it. The docked column stays open; only the phone dock closes on Esc. Covered in `wiring-browser-check`. |
| 2 | "Building ×2" per placement | **Fixed.** `structurePlaced` has no announcer line; the sim event voices it once. Test asserts a count of 1 for placement, deploy and wall drag. |
| 3 | Lava tile seams | **Fixed.** Live lava now fades into the remembered surface over about a tile instead of a rectangular clip. |
| 4 | Tactical Cadet overruns | **Partly fixed.** New `waveCap: 10` for Cadet: measured waves went from 20/18 units (Archive/Fortress) to 9–10, and `ai-doctrine-check` asserts it. **Deferred:** Cadet still out-produces the classic Cadet; that is balance tuning. |
| 5 / 37 | Results screen / debrief | **Fixed.** Two-column table (units built, lost, destroyed; structures built, lost; credits harvested, spent; peak army), plus army and harvest charts. Save, audio, Options and the guide are hidden after the match. |
| 6 | Order hint covers the panel | **Fixed.** On desktop it sits above the panel and group chips. Short landscape screens keep it low, because raised it blocked taps. Phones hide the chips while it shows. |
| 7 | Hover chip over the cameos | **Fixed.** Kept left of the console, flipping to the pointer's left. |
| 8 | Cameo strips keep scroll | **Fixed.** Reset on every new operation. |
| 9 | "Radar offline" silenced by the budget | **Fixed.** It is priority 4 now, outside the budget. |
| 10 | Crate label under the pips | **Fixed.** Drawn after the overlays and higher up. |
| 11 | Units stack when idle; spawn ring | **Deferred.** Older than Wave 1; changing idle separation or exit cells changes movement feel and legacy behaviour and needs a design pass. |
| 12 | "Click to build" on touch | **Fixed:** "Tap to build". **Deferred:** the two-step tap placement, which changes the touch flow and several fixtures. |
| 13 / 34 | Copy and small layout | **Fixed.** Plural segments, ellipsis on long cameo names, every fold turns + into ×, coordinates don't wrap, opaque action sheet. |
| 14 | Splash and rocket kills reveal hidden deaths | **Fixed.** Hidden victims give the team a kill but no rank or promotion (see the note above). Tests added. |
| 15 | Move brackets outline hidden buildings | **Fixed for display:** destination brackets, waypoint markers and patrol turn-backs draw only in sight. **Deferred:** computing the slots from a fog-aware grid would change legacy movement. |
| 16 | Haulers target hidden ore changes | **Fixed with regrowth on.** Haulers use what the player last saw; the memory is saved and validated. |
| 17 | Queued attack reveals a hidden death | **Fixed.** Checking whether the last known point was in sight wasn't enough, because that point is almost always visible. The attack is now marked `lost` while its target is hidden, and a lost target that disappears is walked to like a live one. The QA probe now gives the same result whether the target died or is alive. |
| 18 | Placement reveals hidden units | **Fixed.** `canPlace` and `deploymentStatus` ignore enemy units the team can't see. |
| 19 | Patrols starve pathfinding | **Fixed.** Patrols keep a valid route instead of searching every repath. With 500 patrollers: movers that never moved 168 → 5; 90th-percentile time to first move 151 s → 4 s; step time 28.7 → 14.8 ms. **Not done:** a separate search budget per team. |
| 20 | 2,000 units per side not playable | **Partly fixed.** Target search no longer allocates or sorts (results identical to before in a legacy battle). 2,000 idle units: 51 → 18 ms per step. 1,000 per side in the browser: 2.7 → 14.5 fps, game speed 0.54 → 0.72×. Still below real time at that size. |
| 21 | 2× speed stretches frames | **Fixed.** Stepping stops after 35 ms per frame. 600 per side at 2×: 2.3 → 13.3 fps; at 1×: 4.7 → 17.1 fps. |
| 22 | Saves exceed the browser quota | **Fixed.** A save keeps the newest 2,000 events plus the event counter; ARCHITECTURE now budgets against the ~5.2 M character localStorage limit. |
| 23 | Wave 1 render cost | **Deferred.** Optional profiling, not done. |
| 24 | Units stuck on corners | **Fixed under `crush`** (see the note above). The ASH-001 hauler that retried the path search 832 times now recovers. |
| 25 | Lava too loud at minimum zoom | **Fixed.** Lava chroma 182 → 128 and yellow 17.5% → 0% at minimum zoom; 1.9% yellow on crests at normal zoom. `lava-browser-check` now asks for yellow between 1% and 6% instead of at least 6%. |
| 26 | AI Unity wrecks burn orange | **Fixed.** Blue-white arcs, grey smoke and a faint cold light. |
| 27 | Radar ore looks like unit markers | **Fixed.** Blue and red specks desaturated. |
| 28 | Red crystals look like enemy armour | **Fixed.** Armour is deeper crimson; crystals lean magenta-pink. |
| 29 | Rank plates and badges too big | **Fixed.** Compact below 35 CSS px per tile (20×7 plate, 11 px badge); rank-0 plates at 60%. Group numbers stay visible at every zoom, as AGENTS.md requires. |
| 30 | HiDPI zoom ladder halved | **Fixed** (see the note above). **Deferred:** preparing sprites at 2× resolution, which costs memory and load time on phones. |
| 31 | Phone landscape HUD covers the field | **Fixed.** With the console open, the radar and chips move aside and a unit selection is one row of orders. HUD coverage 54% → 44%. |
| 32 | Held item loses its amber wipe | **Fixed.** |
| 33 | Deploy pushed below the fold | **Fixed.** The opposition line replaces the faction and terrain lines; Deploy is at 619 px of 720 and 798 px of 844. `ai-browser-check` asserts thi
